items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: When Thad left the Basie band in 1962

ctx.x: Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band was a nice career thing for you to do it seems like, and you had some great moments on that record too.

When Thad left the Basie band in 1962 we were neighbors living in the same town. I had known Thad since the 40s from Detroit, Pontiac days you know. Thad lived in Pontiac, I lived in Detroit. And when he left the Basie band he got a gig at Columbia at CBS. His brother Hank was the pianist for Arthur Godfrey and so Hank got Thad a job with the house band there. And it crushed Thad. He had to have a job, but that wasn’t the kind of job — he was hoping it would be something playing jazz. And occasionally Monk would…
just make it up. And then one night Thad came in with an arrangement on this tune. I said, “Thad, isn’t that my tune?” He said no it was mine. He wrote it out.
